paragraphs: Welcome back to GitHub Awesome, your daily dose of the hottest open-source repos lighting up GitHub right now. In this episode of GitHub Trending Today, number eight, we're checking out 22 trending open-source projects that are exploding in popularity. If you love discovering powerful open source like this, smash that like button and let's jump straight into today's trending repos.

TONL is an LLM-friendly serialization format that can cut your data size by up to 50 to 60% compared to JSON, which also means dramatically lower LLM token costs. And unlike binary formats, TONL stays completely human-readable. But TONL isn't just a format; it's a full-blown data platform. You get a JSON path-style query API, CRUD modification tools, hashing and B-tree indexes, and even bit packing for boolean data. It has zero dependencies, is built in pure TypeScript, and is browser-ready at just 10 KB gzipped. Tiny-diffusion, a character-level language diffusion model for text generation, is built as a modified

version of the nanoGPT implementation. But here's the twist: instead of traditional autoregressive generation, this model uses diffusion techniques to generate text character by character. The best part is that this model has only 10.7 million parameters, which means it's incredibly lightweight, easy to experiment with, and runs comfortably on a laptop without a GPU or supercomputer.

You know those multi-line shell commands you copy from docs, blogs, or ChatGPT, and then they don't paste cleanly into your terminal? Yeah, Trimmy fixes that. Trimmy is a tiny macOS menu bar app with one job: paste once, run once. It automatically flattens messy multi-line shell snippets into a clean single-line command that actually runs. There are optional toggles, too, like keeping intentional blank lines or stripping box-drawing characters from fancy prompts.

Next up is an incredibly practical tool for anyone on Windows who needs fast speech-to-text, especially in locked-down corporate environments. This is Chirp, a fully local dictation app powered by Parakeet V3 ST. Parakeet 3 delivers speech recognition accuracy nearly identical to Whisper Large V3. We're talking multilingual 4.1 versus 5.05, but it runs 17x faster and needs no GPU at all, just your CPU. That means Chirp gives you high-end transcription quality without any of the heavy hardware.

ISOBridge is a complete ISO 8583 parser, builder, and forwarder built in .NET 6. If you've ever touched ISO 8583, the decades-old format behind POS transactions, ATMs, and bank switches, you know it's a jungle. Every vendor has its own dialect. The tooling is scattered or proprietary, and debugging messages often feels like reading hieroglyphics. ISOBridge was built to end that pain. It's a fully functional bridge that parses ISO 8583 messages in binary, builds ISO messages cleanly from JSON, and logs every single transaction with full auditability.

Sound Monitor is a noise pollution documentation tool built to record, track, and log excessively loud noises with real evidence you can take to your city council. The goal is simple: if cars are too loud and you need sleep, this app helps you prove it. Sound Monitor continuously records audio from any selected microphone, monitors real-time decibel levels, and automatically logs spikes when noise passes your threshold. It even includes low-frequency detection, targeting that deep 20 to 200 Hz rumble that loud cars and modified exhausts are notorious for.

Stop paying for overpriced email tools you don't even like. Camp just dropped, and it might be the cleanest open-source Mailchimp alternative yet. Camp is a lightweight, self-hosted email marketing platform built entirely in Go. No bloat, no dependency soup. You can send campaigns, manage contacts, segment lists, and track analytics like opens and clicks, all without giving your data to a third party. Create emails with a reusable template system, import or organize your audience, and hit send.

HOPX MCP server is a Model Context Protocol server that gives AI assistants the ability to run real code inside isolated cloud containers safely, quickly, and with full control. It executes Python, JavaScript, Bash, and Go in fully isolated environments complete with pre-installed data science tools like pandas, NumPy, and Matplotlib. It can run system commands, manage files, spin up background processes, and handle long-running tasks, all without touching your local machine.

Horilla CRM is an open-source CRM built for organizations that need serious customer engagement and workflow automation without the complexity of heavyweight commercial systems. You get robust people management with accounts, contacts, and detailed role-based permissions. The sales pipeline includes leads, opportunities, customizable stages, forecasting tools, and even big deal alerts to notify your team when high-value opportunities pop up.

Next on the list is a tool that makes managing traffic feel effortless, especially if you're tired of wrestling with complex YAML files. This is Traefikr, a visual configuration manager that brings simplicity, safety, and clarity to Traefik setups. Instead of manually editing routers, services, and middlewares, Traefikr gives you a clean, guided web interface where every field validates your input in real time. No more indentation mistakes, missing fields, or mysterious config failures.

Next project is a big one for anyone working with Model Context Protocol and hitting token limits or scaling headaches. This is the MCP code execution server, and it tackles one of the biggest pain points in MCP today: context bloat. If you connect Claude to a bunch of MCP servers—say 10, 20, or even 50—each one brings its own tool schemas. Add them up, and suddenly you're burning 30,000 tokens per query before you even type your prompt. That's expensive, slow, and totally unsustainable at scale. This project solves that.

Bring some kawaii energy to your terminal with CliWaifuTamagotchi. It's a CLI anime avatar that lives right in your command line. Dress them up, encourage them, or just let them hang out in background mode. Customize expressions, clothes, and even colors, all saved in your config so your little anime buddy remembers you. Navigate like a Vim master with H, J, K, L keys, and interact every 5 seconds without messy loops. Perfect for coders who want a touch of fun while they grind.

Transform your Minecraft world with Falcraft, the Fabric mod that brings AI-powered 3D generation and texture remixing straight into your game. Generate entire 3D structures just by typing a text prompt—castles, towers, anything you can imagine. Point at a block and watch AI create new designs with perceptual color matching for human vision-accurate results. Textures apply instantly, no restart needed, and background threads keep your game smooth and lag-free.

Meet Flame Haven File Search, making your documents instantly searchable in just minutes. From zero to production in under 5 minutes, with no complex infrastructure and no cloud required. AI-powered semantic search means you can ask natural language questions and get answers linked back to your source documents. PDFs, DocX, all supported up to 50 megabytes. It comes with a Python SDK, REST API, and Swagger UI, plus a one-command Docker deployment with persistence.

EntraMFACheck is the tool that reveals which Azure AD resources still issue tokens without MFA enforcement using the ROPC flow. EntraMFACheck runs ROPC login attempts across dozens of Microsoft cloud resources, checking whether MFA is actually being enforced. If a resource hands out a token with no MFA, you'll see it immediately color-coded as 'MFA not required'. This tool is for authorized testing only, but if you're securing your organization, EntraMFACheck shows you exactly where MFA enforcement is still asleep.

Let's talk about Meridian, a zero-config setup for cloud code that makes AI-assisted development predictable and reliable. Copy two folders, make a couple of scripts executable, and you're done. Meridian preserves context, enforces project rules, and manages tasks and memory, all behind the scenes. No commands, no API keys, no workflow changes—just consistent, deterministic Claude behavior straight from your repo. It's AI development, but without the surprises.

Ever wish reverse engineering was faster, more reliable, and didn't rely on messy Ghidra sessions? Meet Kernagent, the tool that turns any binary into a conversation. It creates a portable snapshot of your binary and lets an AI answer your questions with real evidence, functions, strings, cross-references, and decompiled code. Run it in Docker, CI pipelines, or on your local machine, and get repeatable, auditable results every time. It works with any LLM—OpenAI, Gemini, you name it.

Schengen Visa is a modern TypeScript library for checking Schengen visa appointment availability across 18 countries, giving you embassy contacts, visa requirements, and full document checklists all in one call. The latest version is fast thanks to in-memory caching, dropping repeated check times from 300 milliseconds to just 0.03 milliseconds. Plus, track your success rates, response times, and cache efficiency with built-in stats and performance monitoring.

Agent Evolver is the AI that levels up on its own. It's a self-evolving agent system that learns without you having to teach it. Step one: self-questing. It explores its environment and makes its own tasks, no more manual dataset headaches. Step two: self-navigating. It reuses past experiences to explore smarter and faster—think of it as AI memory on steroids. Step three: self-attributing. It figures out which moves actually matter, giving precise credit to every action.

Ever struggled getting your documents ready for AI retrieval? Meet Rag Chunk, a Python CLI that parses and chunks your Markdown files so your retrieval-augmented generation workflows work flawlessly. Choose from three chunking strategies—fixed size, sliding window, or paragraph—and see which one gives the best results. Want to know how well it works? Rag Chunk evaluates recall with test JSON files so you can benchmark like a pro.

Draggable video controls built with React Native. It's a smooth, interactive video UI with a play button you can drag, and when you move it, the previous and next skip buttons pop out. All powered right on the UI thread for buttery-smooth animations. Enjoy physics-based gestures, springy animations, and a gorgeous glass-style iOS-inspired interface. Full-screen background videos work on both iOS and Android. Every interaction feels responsive and 60 frames per second crisp.

Ever wish you could snap your files away just like Thanos? Meet Thanos, the CLI tool that perfectly deletes half of your files, balanced, as all things should be. Random selection ensures exactly half vanish. But don't worry, safety first: confirm before deletion or do a dry run to see what would go without actually losing anything. Want to include subfolders? It's got recursive support. Plus, a beautiful, colorful CLI with emojis keeps you entertained while it works.
